newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent low sulphur diesel up in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent low sulphur diesel up in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot low sulphur diesel differentials firmed in Chicago Thursday on stronger demand for January barrels and bullish inventory estimates released late in the day, traders said.
"Some good demand emerged for low sulphur in Chicago," one trader said of buying interest that drove bids 1.50 cents a gallon higher to 4.25 cents under the print.

Midwest refineries last week were operating at 92.2 percent of capacity, down 2.6 percentage points from the prior week and well off a blistering pace of recent weeks, the American Petroleum Institute said.

Distillate stocks were 313,000 barrels below the prior week's levels, fueled by a 456,000 barrel draw in low sulphur diesel stocks on the week. That draw was partly offset by a 143,000 barrel build in high sulphur diesel inventories.
Gasoline inventories in the PADD II Midwest were 835,000 barrels below the prior week and 2.45 million barrels below the same week last year, the trade group said.
Unleaded gasoline remained bid 2.75 cents a gallon under NYMEX February unleaded for January deliveries in Chicago and 2.50 cents under the print in Group Three, traders said.
High sulphur diesel for January deliveries was talked 6.0 cents a gallon under NYMEX February heating oil in Chicago and 7.50 cents under the print in Group Three.
